rationales: Bu Ali Sina is renowned for medical works, not Al-Haywan.
Aristotle wrote works on animals, but Al-Haywan is attributed to Abdul Malik Asmai in this context.
Abdul Malik Asmai is the expected author of Al-Haywan.
Jabir Bin Hayan is associated with chemistry, not this book.
Aristotle was an earlier naturalist, not the scientist who formed the theory of evolution by reading other naturalists’ works.
Darwin developed his theory of evolution after studying the work of other naturalists.
Laveran is known for identifying the malaria parasite, not for developing the theory of evolution.
Ronald Ross is known for work on malaria transmission, not for developing the theory of evolution.
Monera are prokaryotic organisms, not multicellular eukaryotic consumers.
Protista are mostly unicellular and do not fit the description of multicellular consumers.
Plantae are mainly photosynthetic producers, not consumers.
Animalia includes multicellular eukaryotic consumers.
Ribosomes use rRNA but do not form it.
Mitochondria are not the site where ribosomal RNA is formed.
The nucleolus is the site of ribosomal RNA formation.
Vacuoles do not form ribosomal RNA.
Germ line cells are eukaryotic and can undergo mitosis, but mitosis is not limited to them.
Prokaryotic cells divide by binary fission rather than mitosis.
Mitosis occurs in eukaryotic cells.
Bacteria are prokaryotic and do not undergo mitosis.
Ribosome synthesis is not the key process whose inhibition directly prevents entry into mitosis.
Protein synthesis in G2 supplies proteins needed for mitosis, so its inhibition can prevent mitosis.
Chromosomes are duplicated in S phase, not G2.
Enzyme synthesis is not the specific expected answer; protein synthesis is the required process.
Vitamins are not products of lipid digestion by lipase.
Lipase breaks lipids into fatty acids and glycerol.
Glycogen is a carbohydrate, not a product of lipid digestion.
Glucose is produced by carbohydrate digestion, not lipid digestion.
About 1% of the light falling on a leaf surface is absorbed for photosynthesis.
About 2% is not the stated approximate amount absorbed.
About 3% is not the stated approximate amount absorbed.
About 15% is not the stated approximate amount absorbed.
Arteries generally lack valves along their length, although some have valves at their exits from the heart.
Veins have valves that help prevent the backflow of blood.
Capillaries do not have valves.
Muscles are not blood vessels and do not have blood-flow valves.
Milk does not typically contain 10% lipid.
Milk does not typically contain 12% lipid.
A lipid content of 0.9% is lower than the usual value given for milk.
Milk contains about 4% lipid in the stated textbook value.
Loss of electrons from an atom is oxidation.
Reduction is gain of electrons.
Dehydration is the removal of water.
Respiration is a cellular process, not the name for electron loss.
Jabir Bin Hayan is credited in this context with first giving the concept of metabolism.
Koshland is associated with later work on enzyme mechanisms, not the first concept of metabolism.
Ibn-e-Nafeez is known for describing pulmonary circulation, not for first giving this concept.
Bu Ali Sina is renowned for medical contributions, not for first giving the concept of metabolism.
Cytokinesis is the division of the cytoplasm.
Division of the nucleus is called karyokinesis.
Chromosomes separate during nuclear division; this is not the meaning of cytokinesis.
Cytokinesis does not mean division of mitochondria.
Meiosis comes from a Greek word meaning to make smaller or lessen.
To make larger is not the meaning of meiosis.
To cut is not the meaning of meiosis.
To duplicate is not the meaning of meiosis.
0.1 cm is 1 mm, larger than the stated resolving power of the human eye.
0.1 μm is far finer than the resolving power of the unaided human eye.
The human eye can resolve objects about 0.1 mm apart under suitable conditions.
0.1 dm is 1 cm, much larger than the stated resolving power.
